gloss: to come apart at the seams; to break into a smile; to begin to bloom

definitions.gloss: to come apart at the seams; to become undone
definitions.explanation: For stitching or fabric to come loose or fall apart.

definitions.gloss: to break into a smile; to relax one's expression
definitions.explanation: For one's face to soften into a smile, as if the tightness is coming undone.

definitions.gloss: to begin to bloom; to start opening (of flowers)
definitions.explanation: For flower buds to begin opening.

examples.japanese: {縫|ぬ}い{目|め}が{綻|ほころ}びている。
{古|ふる}いコートの{袖|そで}が{綻|ほころ}びてきた。
examples.english: The sleeves of my old coat are coming apart.

examples.japanese: {何年|なんねん}も{着|き}ているジャケットの{縫|ぬ}い{目|め}がところどころ{綻|ほころ}びている。
examples.english: The seams of the jacket I've been wearing for years are coming apart in places.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}の{顔|かお}が{思|おも}わず{綻|ほころ}んだ。
examples.english: Her face broke into an involuntary smile.

examples.japanese: プレゼントを{見|み}て{子供|こども}の{顔|かお}が{綻|ほころ}んだ。
examples.english: The child's face lit up when they saw the present.

examples.japanese: {緊張|きんちょう}していた{彼|かれ}の{表情|ひょうじょう}が、{温|あたた}かい{言葉|ことば}を{聞|き}いてようやく{綻|ほころ}んだ。
examples.english: His tense expression finally softened into a smile when he heard the warm words.

examples.japanese: {桜|さくら}の{蕾|つぼみ}が{綻|ほころ}び{始|はじ}めた。
examples.english: The cherry blossom buds are beginning to bloom.

examples.japanese: {梅|うめ}の{花|はな}が{綻|ほころ}ぶと、{春|はる}の{訪|おとず}れを{感|かん}じる。
examples.english: When the plum blossoms start to open, you can feel spring arriving.

examples.japanese: {長|なが}い{冬|ふゆ}が{終|お}わり、{庭|にわ}のあちこちで{花|はな}が{綻|ほころ}び{始|はじ}めた。
examples.english: The long winter ended, and flowers began to bloom here and there in the garden.

notes:
VERB TYPE:
{自動詞|じどうし} (intransitive verb)
Ichidan verb ({一段動詞|いちだんどうし}/{上一段|かみいちだん})

CONJUGATION:
・{綻|ほころ}びない (negative)
・{綻|ほころ}びて (te-form)
・{綻|ほころ}びた (past)

NOUN FORM:
{綻|ほころ}び - a flaw, coming apart, crack (in a plan or facade)

LITERARY USE:
This verb is often used poetically, especially for describing smiles breaking through a stern expression or flowers starting to bloom in spring.
